ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in an equilateral $\triangle ABC$, points $E$ and $D$ are located on sides $AC$ and $BC$, respectively, with $AE=CD$. Lines $AD$ and $BE$ intersect at point $O$. $\triangle ABE \cong \triangle CAD$; If $\angle OBD=45^\circ$, find the measure of $\angle ADC$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From (1) we have $\triangle ABE \cong \triangle CAD$,\\
$\therefore \angle ABE = \angle CAD$,\\
$\therefore \angle BOD = \angle ABE + \angle BAO = \angle BAC = 60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ADC = \angle OBD + \angle BOD = 45^\circ + 60^\circ = \boxed{105^\circ}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, in an equilateral $\triangle ABC$, points $E$ and $D$ are located on sides $AC$ and $BC$, respectively, with $AE=CD$. Lines $AD$ and $BE$ intersect at point $O$. $\triangle ABE \cong \triangle CAD$; If $\angle OBD=45^\circ$, find the measure of $\angle ADC$.
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} From (1) we have $\triangle ABE \cong \triangle CAD$,\\ $\therefore \angle ABE = \angle CAD$,\\ $\therefore \angle BOD = \angle ABE + \angle BAO = \angle BAC = 60^\circ$,\\ $\therefore \angle ADC = \angle OBD + \angle BOD = 45^\circ + 60^\circ = \boxed{105^\circ}$
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure is a large triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right; E is marked on side AC, D is marked on side BC. Segment BE and segment AD intersect at interior point O, therefore O is on BE; D is on BC, so viewed from B, ray BO and BE are in the same direction, ray BD and BC are in the same direction.
Reasoning: It is known that ∠OBD=45°. Because BO and BE are collinear, BD and BC are collinear, ∠OBD is ∠EBC=45°. △ABC is an equilateral triangle, therefore ∠ABC=60°. In the figure BE is located inside ∠ABC, so ∠ABE=60°−45°=15°. Also from the known △ABE≅△CAD, corresponding angles are equal, obtaining ∠CAD=∠ABE=15°. Because D is on BC, ∠ACD=∠ACB=60°. In △ACD, ∠ADC=180°−∠CAD−∠ACD=180°−15°−60°=105°.
